name: Millennial socialism
summary: Millennial socialism is the revival of support for democratic socialism and social democracy among Americans and Britons born roughly 1981 to 1996. It centers on health care as a right, higher taxes on the wealthy, living wages, free public college and student-debt relief, tighter regulation of finance and corporate money in politics, and climate action, mostly pursued through elections. Surveys and commentators describe it as a demand for a Nordic-style welfare state and a fairer economy, not state ownership of industry.
scope: Generational political attitudes of US millennials as expressed by Bernie Sanders's democratic socialism (Georgetown speech, 2015), the Ocasio-Cortez wing, and polling analysis (Pew, Reason-Rupe). It is a trend with no founding text or party program, so most positions beyond economic policy are inferred and marked low. It excludes Marxist-Leninist and revolutionary socialism.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Sanders calls health care a right and backs Medicare-for-all; relief from health costs is a named millennial-socialist demand.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Sanders's speech calls for a $15 minimum wage so full-time workers do not live in poverty.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Adherents accept private business but blame greed and corporate power for inequality; Pew finds the system seen as favoring the powerful.

public-ownership.rationale: Sanders says government should not own the means of production, and Ekins finds young people want a safety net, not state-run firms, though some back public utilities.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Sanders demands that the wealthy and big corporations pay their fair share, and the Nordic-style high-tax model is the stated reference point.

unions-good.rationale: Sanders's speech lists collective bargaining among New Deal gains and the cohort favors labor, but the sources give no direct union statement.

property-fundamental.rationale: Inferred from distrust of inherited wealth and corporate power; sources do not discuss property rights directly.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Sanders attacks deregulation won by Wall Street lobbying and bailouts, and Pew finds millennials most likely to say the system favors the powerful.

cut-welfare.rationale: The trend is defined by demand for a wider safety net, so cutting welfare is rejected.

worker-ownership.rationale: Sanders rejects state ownership of production but the sources say nothing on worker cooperatives; adherents are split.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred from civil-libertarian leanings of the Sanders-Ocasio-Cortez left; not covered in sources.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from Sanders's criticism of mass incarceration and the cohort's liberal social views; not directly sourced.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Adherents split between anti-prejudice commitments and free-speech instincts; sources silent.

strong-leader.rationale: Sanders stresses a mass democratic movement and voting rights; inferred, not stated.

state-harmful.rationale: The trend wants a bigger state role in health, education and safety net, so calling the state harmful is the opposite of its stance.

limit-guns.rationale: Inferred from the Democratic-left alignment of the Sanders and Ocasio-Cortez coalition; not in the sources.

empower-police-military.rationale: Sanders calls $80 billion yearly on incarceration wasteful and backs Black Lives Matter, implying shifting money from policing.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are divided between decriminalization and abolitionist feminist views.

decide-locally.rationale: The programs it wants (national health care, free college) are national; inferred.

rehabilitation.rationale: Sanders argues jobs and education for young people beat spending on incarceration.

traditional-family.rationale: Inferred from the cohort's socially liberal profile; sources do not discuss family.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Inferred from the liberal social views of the cohort and its leaders; not discussed in the sources.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed in Sanders's speech; inferred from the progressive profile of its figures.

more-religion-public.rationale: Inferred; the sources do not discuss religion.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Sanders backs Black Lives Matter and equal treatment for African Americans, and the left-leaning cohort treats racial justice as a core concern.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from progressive cultural positions; sources silent.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Sanders opposes appeals to nativism; otherwise inferred.

gradual-change.rationale: Sanders calls for a political revolution-style movement for big change, but adherents mostly work through elections; inferred.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Sanders backs a path to citizenship and opposes nativist appeals.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Sanders proposes a coalition-based approach to ISIS but the sources do not address UN powers.

free-trade.rationale: Inferred from distrust of corporate power; sources do not discuss trade.

nation-first.rationale: Sanders favors coalitions and force as a last resort; inferred.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Sanders treats military force as a last resort; the cohort is not interventionist, but the sources do not address human-rights intervention.

open-borders.rationale: Sanders backs reform and citizenship paths, not open borders; adherents split.

limit-growth.rationale: Sanders ties climate action to regulation, not shrinking growth; inferred.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Sanders calls for government action against fossil-fuel profiteering and climate change, and capitalism is linked in the cohort to climate harm.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Inferred from environmental left norms; unsourced.

revolution-justified.rationale: The movement pursues change through elections and a democratic socialism that Sanders rooted in American democracy.

central-planning.rationale: Sanders rejects state ownership of production and Ekins finds young people do not want an economy managed by government.

socialized-markets.rationale: Not discussed; adherents accept private business and have no settled view on worker-owned markets.

land-value-tax.rationale: No source ties the trend to land taxation; neutral because the idea is absent from its tax debate, which centers on wealth and estates.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Sanders targets estate tax loopholes, and inherited wealth is cited as a grievance of the cohort.

basic-income.rationale: Not addressed in sources; adherents prefer targeted programs and jobs but some favor UBI.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Inferred from calls for green and public investment; not stated in sources.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The trend wants less wealth concentration but no source endorses a small-owner economy as the remedy, so neutral.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Adherents want higher wages and jobs; Sanders's agenda assumes a market economy with wages.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: No source supports it; contrary to a state-managed welfare agenda.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Not part of the discourse; inferred.

one-party-rule.rationale: The movement operates through democratic politics; Sanders calls for one person one vote and public election funding.

democracy-best.rationale: Sanders's democratic socialism centers on voting rights and democratic accountability.

workers-councils.rationale: Not part of the movement's program; inferred.

right-to-secede.rationale: Secession is not part of the trend's agenda and adherents have no common view of it.

political-violence-never.rationale: The movement is electoral; no source addresses violence directly.

war-builds-character.rationale: Sanders treats force as a last resort; inferred.

military-superiority.rationale: Inferred from criticism of military spending and last-resort view of force.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Adherents frame politics as ordinary people versus the wealthy few but rarely adopt Marxist historical theory; sources silent.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Aims to reduce inequality, but sources frame goals as rights and fairness, not equal outcomes.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Reparations for colonialism are not in the sources; adherents might favor them on racial-justice grounds but no position is documented.

civilizational-union.rationale: Not part of this outlook; inferred.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Sanders criticizes greed as policy driver; inferred.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Rights-based framing (health care as a right); inferred.

limit-population.rationale: Inferred weakly: the trend blames economic arrangements, not numbers, for hardship, so active population limits are disfavored.

accelerate-technology.rationale: The sources are silent on technology policy, and adherents split between tech optimism and worry about job disruption.

human-enhancement.rationale: Bodily enhancement is outside the trend's documented concerns, so no side is taken.

restore-past-order.rationale: The trend is forward-looking reform driven by the cohort's grievances over costs and debt.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Not addressed; Ekins argues the cohort is pragmatic about outcomes, but adherents identify with socialism.

direct-action.rationale: The movement works largely through elections and primaries.

means-match-ends.rationale: Democratic means for democratic socialism is implied by Sanders's speech.

return-to-foraging.rationale: A reformist welfare-state movement in an industrial economy has no sympathy for abandoning agriculture and industry.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Sanders's program assumes jobs, wages and private business, so abolishing the division of labor is far from it.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Health and education as rights suggest need-based provision in some areas, but not a general principle in sources.

production-for-use.rationale: Sanders supports private business that profits and grows; adherents split.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Capitalism is tied to greed, but Sanders explicitly rewards business success; no stated theory of exploitation.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Sanders and the cohort tie socialism to democracy; Ekins notes the cohort rejects state control.

collective-farming.rationale: No source proposes collectivizing farms; the trend explicitly stops short of government ownership of production.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Capitalism is blamed for inequality and climate harm in the cohort but no source claims it inevitably causes great-power war.

taxation-theft.rationale: The movement is organized around higher taxes to fund public goods.

harm-principle.rationale: Liberal-left adherents might accept it, yet a regulatory agenda restricts adult conduct beyond harm to others, and sources are silent.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Sanders emphasizes voting rights and democratic voice.

state-as-business.rationale: Government is seen as providing rights, not customer service.

media-academia-power.rationale: Inferred; corporate rather than media power is the focus.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Sanders condemns prejudice and backs racial equality.

organic-representation.rationale: The trend works through parties and primaries, so representation by families and trade bodies is foreign to it.

total-state.rationale: Democratic socialism here is explicitly not state ownership of production.

national-rebirth.rationale: Millennial socialists seek policy reform of existing institutions, not a national rebirth from decadence.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Inferred from Sanders's last-resort view of force.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Oaths between lords and followers contradict the movement's one-person-one-vote democracy.

universal-morality.rationale: Adherents speak of rights as universal, but sources give no philosophical position on universal moral truths.

single-common-good.rationale: Politics framed as the many versus powerful interests.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Adherents are split in the cohort; not addressed in sources.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not part of the trend's documented concerns; adherents are split along differing views on specific cases.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival is not a topic in the sources, so neutral.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Inferred from democratic socialist branding and the DSA's growth; sources do not state it.

school-vouchers.rationale: Inferred from preference for public education (free public college).

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Inferred from the large spending agenda.

rule-by-example.rationale: Sanders stresses laws, programs and voting rights rather than rulers' moral example, so mild disagreement is inferred.

national-self-determination.rationale: The sources do not discuss national self-determination, and adherents' views vary by case.

force-without-un.rationale: Force as last resort; coalition approach.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The sources do not discuss epistemology; adherents range from secular to religious progressives.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Inferred from Sanders's opposition to nativism.

positive-liberty.rationale: Health care, education and living wages are framed as rights that give people real freedom.

class-collaboration.rationale: Frames billionaires and Wall Street as adversaries; inferred.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Nothing in the trend suggests destroying cultural institutions, and its policies fund public libraries and education.

dominated-front.rationale: Anti-Western fronts are absent from the trend, and adherents hold mixed views on foreign policy.

workers-nation.rationale: Sanders's coalition-minded view of world affairs and its class language point away from organizing by nation, though weakly.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Sanders criticizes the lack of paid leave for mothers and supports gender equality.

ban-interest.rationale: Interest bans are not on the agenda; the trend focuses on student debt relief and Wall Street, not abolishing lending.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Sanders backs equal treatment and Black Lives Matter.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Not addressed; adherents see the state as capturable by elections.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Sanders attacks fossil-fuel profiteering that harms the environment.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Sanders backs a path to citizenship and opposes nativism, so demanding cultural assimilation is disfavored.

national-mission.rationale: No source suggests spreading a national form of government, and Sanders treats force as a last resort.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Sanders attacks lobbying and big-money politics and calls to overturn Citizens United.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Black Lives Matter support and criticism of incarceration imply support for holding security forces to account.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The movement is about expanding government provision.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Equal treatment and rights for all are central to Sanders's speech.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Marxist-debate question not relevant to the cohort.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The sources never address it and adherents are divided in views on settler-colonial framings.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Religion-based personal law is not a topic in the sources, so neutral.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Inferred from civil-liberties leanings; the trend is not documented as favoring legal limits on religion.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A religiously motivated ban is far from the trend's economic and social-justice agenda.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Religion in schools is not discussed; the mild agreement is inferred from the secular-leaning progressive coalition.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist state-theory question that the electoral millennial trend does not engage; mildly disfavored.

consent-of-governed.rationale: One person one vote and democratic accountability are core to Sanders's democratic framing.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: A postmodern epistemic claim the sources do not connect to the trend, so neutral.

trade-surplus.rationale: Export surpluses are not part of the trend's economic debate.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Sanders limits force to a last resort, yet the sources do not state an absolute principle, so neutral.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Outlawing parties conflicts with democratic openness, though the sources are silent; mild disagreement inferred.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Inferred from concern with the power of the wealthy.

separated-powers.rationale: Constitutional design is not addressed in the sources, and adherents have no shared view.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Focus on poverty wages, health costs and student debt.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Sanders opposes nativism and prejudice, and the cohort is the most diverse generation, so the claim is rejected.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Sortition is not part of the trend's democratic reform agenda, which stresses voting and campaign finance.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Suspending legal protections contradicts the civil-liberties and democratic commitments Sanders sets out.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price caps are not discussed in the sources; adherents might back them for housing but not food rationing.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Pay limits for representatives are not part of the documented trend.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: The movement is a loose primary-driven coalition rather than a disciplined party, so binding discipline is disfavored.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Not addressed; UK-linked adherents lean EU-friendly but not documented.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Presidential control of forces and ministers is not discussed; mild disagreement is inferred from the stress on democratic accountability.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is irrelevant to the trend, so neutral.

clerical-rule.rationale: Rule by religious scholars contradicts the democratic principles Sanders stresses.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: The trend does not take the revolutionary-defeatist line, though it is skeptical of war; mildly disfavored.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Censorship for morals is incompatible with the liberal social views of the cohort.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Open-ended incumbency fits poorly with the movement's anti-establishment tone; inferred.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall is not discussed in the sources, so no stance is documented.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Sanders proposes coalition-based action against ISIS, but the sources say nothing on ending alliances.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Cost-of-living concerns point to tenant protection and affordability, not a ban on renting.

people-in-arms.rationale: An armed citizenry in place of an army clashes with the gun-control leanings of the left.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The cohort is urban-leaning and the sources do not romanticize rural life.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Not covered by the sources, and adherents have no shared view.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Inferred from the progressive, anti-prejudice outlook; cultural relativism itself is not discussed in the sources.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Inferred from the liberal social outlook of the cohort and its leaders; no source discusses curricula.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Teaching creationism conflicts with the secular, science-respecting progressive outlook, inferred without direct sources.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Inferred from civil-libertarian leanings of the cohort; pornography is not discussed in the sources.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Inferred from path to citizenship stance.

minority-language-support.rationale: The sources do not discuss language policy, and the trend has no documented stance.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Exemptions pit religious liberty against general law and adherents are split; sources are silent.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Inferred from the socially liberal outlook of the cohort; the sources do not discuss conformity.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Student debt relief is a priority but foreign debt not addressed.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: A decolonization-era question not found in the sources on the trend.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Constitutional rewriting is not on the movement's agenda, which stresses election reform instead.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Inferred from the egalitarian and anti-poverty orientation; sources address domestic poverty, not foreign aid.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Skepticism of military spending suggests opposition to extra nuclear forces, inferred and unsourced.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Voting reform emphasis suggests it; inferred.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Sanders attacks Wall Street, but sources give no stance on central bank independence.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial concessions are not addressed in the sources and adherents differ.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A Marxist-theory debate the cohort does not engage with.

collective-defense.rationale: Alliances like NATO are not discussed in the sources; Sanders favors coalitions, but not as binding commitments.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Annexation disputes are outside the trend's documented concerns.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Church-state curbs are not part of the trend's program.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: A ceremonial head of state is not a topic in the US-centered sources.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Inferred from Sanders's last-resort view of force, which suggests mild disagreement.

region-keeps-system.rationale: A one-country-two-systems question absent from the sources; neutral.

sacred-ruler.rationale: A sacred ruler is the opposite of the egalitarian democratic stance Sanders sets out.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Sanders and Nordic-style progressive high personal taxation are the reference.

character-from-environment.rationale: Inferred from emphasis on circumstances and opportunity.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Rulers above law contradicts the democratic accountability themes in Sanders's speech on money in politics.

space-expansion.rationale: Spending on space is not a priority of the trend, which targets health, education and wages; mild disagreement inferred.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical constitutional theory is not discussed, so neutral.

leader-cult.rationale: Mass praise of a leader as embodiment of the nation conflicts with the movement's grassroots and democratic self-image.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody rules are not addressed by the sources.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A debate within ruling communist parties that the trend does not engage.

land-redistribution.rationale: Land seizure is outside the trend, which mostly concerns taxes and services in an urban industrial economy.

refugee-return.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, and adherents lack a common view.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Territorial claims based on nationality conflict with the anti-nativist stance of the trend.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Penalties for leaving a religion contradict liberal freedom-of-conscience norms shared by the cohort.

women-must-cover.rationale: A legal dress mandate is the opposite of the trend's commitment to gender equality.

common-currency.rationale: The sources do not discuss monetary union.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Ethnic and linguistic unification is foreign to the trend and clashes with its opposition to nativism.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: A multinational-state question not covered by the sources.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Not covered by the sources, so no position is documented.

ban-cartels.rationale: Inferred from anti-monopoly and Wall Street criticism.

no-bailouts.rationale: Sanders criticizes bailouts of financial firms without consequences for executives.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The trend wants to overturn Citizens United through courts and law, so it does not simply defer to majorities; inferred.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Inferred from progressive commitments to gender equality; no source states a quota stance.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Reserving economic life for the majority conflicts with the anti-nativist, equal-treatment stance of the movement.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Inferred from labor and climate priorities.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Nation-centered history teaching is not an aim of the trend, and the cohort leans cosmopolitan.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Rule of one society over another contradicts egalitarian and anti-prejudice commitments.

patriotic-education.rationale: Loyalty-and-pride schooling is not part of the trend; mild disagreement inferred.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary reform is not mentioned in the sources.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The sources neither claim capitalism will collapse nor that it can adapt; adherents differ.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Post-imperial influence-seeking conflicts with Sanders's last-resort view of force and coalition approach; inferred.

delink-world-market.rationale: Adherents want fairer trade rules, not economic withdrawal; the sources say nothing about delinking.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist thesis that the trend does not take up.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Constitutional design is not discussed, so no stance is documented.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: A decolonization question absent from the sources.

elective-rulers.rationale: Inferred from the stress on one person one vote and democratic voice.

minority-veto.rationale: Consent-based vetoes would block the national programs the trend wants; inferred from policy goals.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: A classical resistance-theory question that the sources do not address.

parliament-supreme.rationale: A Westminster-style question absent from the US-centered sources.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Inferred from progressive values and climate concern; the sources do not mention animals.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal use is not discussed, and adherents divide between welfare reform and abolition.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Framed as rights and taxation, not charity.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: A critical-theory claim not found in the sources; adherents hold varied views.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: A Gramscian argument that the sources on the trend do not address.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Dependency theory is not part of the trend's documented ideas.

native-born-offices.rationale: Reserving offices for the native born conflicts with anti-nativism and the path-to-citizenship stance.

party-own-road.rationale: A communist-party question the trend does not engage.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Inferred from the egalitarian, aid-friendly leaning of the left; sources are silent on development policy.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Irredentism conflicts with Sanders's last-resort view of force.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Political leadership by descent clashes with equal-rights commitments, and no source supports it.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Inferred from the anti-prejudice outlook of the movement; constitutional founding values are not discussed.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Cohort less shaped by Cold War memory per Ekins; adherents split.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Sanders's racial-justice stance and condemnation of prejudice make this historical claim unwelcome; inferred.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred from racial-justice commitments, which would favor removal or recontextualizing monuments of condemned figures.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not discussed in the sources, and adherents are split.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: No source addresses it, and adherents split between symmetry and gendered-violence views.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Inferred from universalist commitments to democracy and equal rights found in Sanders's speech.

military-guardian-role.rationale: A political role for the army contradicts the democratic emphasis of the movement.

paid-care-work.rationale: Sanders criticizes lack of paid leave; wider care pay inferred.

filial-duty.rationale: Family duties are not discussed in the sources.

office-by-exam.rationale: Civil-service examination is not discussed, so no stance is documented.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Not discussed; adherents mix distrust of corporations with internationalism.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from liberal social views of the cohort; not discussed in the sources.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Binding mandates for leaders are not part of the trend's reform ideas.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Defends Social Security-style public programs; Glaeser frames the trend as built on them.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Use-based land tenure is not a demand of the trend, which respects private housing ownership.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The sources do not discuss budget procedure.

single-official-language.rationale: Enforcing one language conflicts with the inclusive, pro-immigrant stance; inferred.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Land-ownership limits on foreigners clash with the anti-nativist stance, though the sources are silent.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred from last-resort view of force.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Sanders limits force to a last resort and has criticized interventions, so invading an allied state is disfavored.

corporate-influence.rationale: Sanders attacks lobbying and big money in politics and calls for overturning Citizens United.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from civil-liberties concern; the sources do not discuss foreign funding of NGOs.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Fertility incentives are not discussed; adherents favor family support such as paid leave but not pronatalism as such.

residents-only-property.rationale: Limits on home purchases are not covered in the sources, and adherents are divided.

job-guarantee.rationale: Inferred from the Sanders/Ocasio-Cortez agenda; not in the sources opened.

democratic-peace.rationale: The thesis is not addressed in the sources, and adherents differ on democracy promotion.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Philosophical anarchism-style claim not discussed by the sources.

non-intervention.rationale: Sanders treats force as last resort but proposes coalition action on ISIS, so absolute non-intervention is not his line.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is not discussed in the sources.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Same-sex marriage rights and family benefits are expected to stay; abolishing legal marriage is inferred as disfavored.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred from the democratic transparency theme in the push against money in politics.

local-production.rationale: Localism is not a stated aim; the trend stresses national programs.

informal-organisation.rationale: The movement builds mass campaigns and organizations such as the DSA, which has about 100,000 members, not informal affinity groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Inferred from internationalist leanings; no source states a view.

religious-nation.rationale: Defining the nation by religion contradicts opposition to prejudice and nativism.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Tribute and ritual submission is far from the movement's democratic and egalitarian approach to foreign relations.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Sanders explicitly supports private enterprise and ownership of personal property is untouched.

defeat-communism.rationale: Cohort lacks Cold War memory (Ekins); inferred.

religion-illusion.rationale: A Marxist claim about religion that the cohort does not adopt; sources are silent.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Capitalism is linked to greed, climate change and inequality in the cohort.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred from paid leave and care emphasis.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Linguistic purism is foreign to the trend.

treaties-binding.rationale: Indigenous or minority treaties are not discussed in the sources, though adherents might favor honoring them.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Sanders endorses a market economy with a welfare state, not small property-sharing communes.

majority-settlement.rationale: Encouraging settlement to shift demographics contradicts anti-nativist commitments.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Social democracy as third way is Pethokoukis and Ekins's framing; adherents differ.

historical-land-claim.rationale: The sources do not address land claims, and adherents differ across particular conflicts.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Denial contradicts the condemnation of prejudice in Sanders's speech and is rejected by mainstream progressives.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Cohort and leaders support equality; Sanders opposes prejudice.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Legal punishment for blasphemy conflicts with liberal freedom-of-expression norms.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Exploitative colonial governance is the opposite of the trend's egalitarian outlook.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: A religious-law question that does not apply to the trend and which the sources never mention.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Armed removal of secular rulers is the opposite of the electoral, democratic approach of the movement.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Inferred from alliance of class and racial justice themes in Sanders's speech.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Inferred from the progressive profile of the cohort and its leaders; no source states it.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not discussed in the sources, and adherents are split.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Adherents identify with the left; the trend is defined by left-wing economics, so the claim is mildly rejected.

alienated-labor.rationale: Marxist theory of alienation is not adopted by the sources on the trend; they stress wages and security.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Sanders proposes working with Muslim nations and opposes prejudice.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Authority resting on God conflicts with Sanders's popular-sovereignty framing of democracy.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Not discussed in the sources, and adherents split between secularism and religious freedom.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Inferred from progressive support for worker protections; no source addresses NDAs.

social-market-economy.rationale: Commentators describe the trend as support for Nordic-style social democracy: markets plus a strong welfare state.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Sanders views force as a last resort, not abolishable; the sources show no pacifist demand.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Great-power bloc politics is not discussed in the sources.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Hereditary succession of leaders contradicts one person one vote and anti-inheritance sentiment.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Mutual banking is not part of the trend's documented ideas.

property-franchise.rationale: Sanders calls for one person, one vote and easier voter participation, which excludes wealth-based voting limits.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ecofeminist claim not addressed in the sources.

reification.rationale: A Marxist-philosophical concept that the trend does not use.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Inferred from concern with money in politics.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Rule-of-law procedure is not discussed in the sources.

racial-franchise.rationale: His speech stresses equal treatment for African Americans and voting rights for all, which excludes race-limited voting.

online-participation.rationale: Digital democracy is not part of the trend's documented reforms.

open-government-data.rationale: Not discussed in the sources, though the transparency theme may imply support.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Marriage restrictions by religion contradict the anti-prejudice, equal-rights outlook.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Targeting a religious minority's businesses is the sort of prejudice Sanders condemns.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Sortition assemblies are not part of the trend's documented ideas.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Doctrinal reform is not a political topic in the sources.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Sanders argues concentrated wealth distorts politics and billionaires dominate; Pew finds millennials most likely to say the system favors the powerful.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred from the liberal social outlook; the sources do not discuss military policy on this.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: State-promoted atheism is rejected by a democratic, liberal-leaning movement, though sources are silent.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Sanders cuts incarceration spending but does not call for abolition.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Consociational models are not discussed in the sources.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The trend wants state provision rather than charity.

term-limits.rationale: Term limits are not part of the documented agenda.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid democracy is not discussed by the sources.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Not mentioned; adherents prioritize climate, health and economic issues over extinction risk specifically.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred from gender-equality commitments; religious office is not discussed in the sources.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred from gender equality and Sanders's concern over paid leave for mothers.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; adherents are divided.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred from cost-of-living grievances of the cohort.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred as disfavored: the trend does not target patents or copyright, though it attacks drug-industry power.

uniformed-youth.rationale: State-drilled youth movements are alien to the democratic movement.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Not discussed in the sources, so no stance.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; adherents are divided on US bases abroad.

recognise-genocide.rationale: The sources do not address it, and adherents differ across specific cases.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Inferred from concern with inherited wealth and fair wages.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Sanders accepts force as a last resort, which implies self-defense is not wrong; adherents are not documented as pacifists.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Primordial nationalism conflicts with the cosmopolitan outlook of the cohort, inferred.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Academic gender-theory claim not addressed by the sources.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: A feminist-theory dispute that the sources do not address.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Sacred honors for national martyrs clash with the movement's outlook; inferred.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The trend frames politics as economic fairness, not a spiritual battle of good and evil.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: A Zionist-theory question that the sources do not address.

culture-before-state.rationale: Cultural nationalism is not part of the trend, whose focus is state programs and policy; inferred.

god-not-male.rationale: A theological question not addressed by the sources.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: A theological question not addressed by the sources.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: A boundary-politics question not covered by the sources.

independent-unions.rationale: Inferred: the movement's pro-labor stance is not tied to a party or state, so independence is likely valued.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist test of socialism that the trend does not apply.

second-chamber.rationale: Not discussed in the sources, so no stance.

municipal-property.rationale: Neither Sanders nor commentators propose local community ownership of production.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Libertarian-municipalist idea not found in the sources.

family-wage.rationale: Living-wage framing supports a wage able to sustain a family; not stated in family terms.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; adherents attack drug pricing, not approval speed.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Not discussed in the sources, so no stance.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; adherents split on cryptocurrency.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred from civil-libertarian leanings of the cohort; the sources say nothing about online identity.

person-over-state.rationale: Sanders frames rights as personal entitlements, yet sources do not take a view on the state serving persons as ends.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Not discussed in the sources, and adherents range from secular to religious.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Federal structure is not discussed in the sources.

gm-crops.rationale: Not discussed in the sources, and environmental-left adherents are split on GM crops.

dense-cities.rationale: Not discussed in the sources, although climate-minded adherents may favor density.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Sanders appeals to common class interests while condemning prejudice, so organizing by race is not his line; inferred.

racial-pride.rationale: Racial pride is not discussed in the sources, and adherents are split.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Inferred from Sanders's last-resort view of force.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Language-based nationhood is foreign to the civic outlook of the trend.

communal-electorates.rationale: Separate religious electorates contradict one person one vote, which Sanders stresses.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Conspiratorial claims of foreign partition plots are not part of the trend.

free-public-college.rationale: Sanders says anyone qualified should attend public colleges tuition-free, and student debt relief is a named demand.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Sanders wants climate action but the sources do not say whether through taxes or regulation, so neutral.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Essentialist claims about women's values are not documented in the sources.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred from transparency themes; secret treaties are not discussed in the sources.

capital-controls.rationale: Not discussed, though Sanders's Wall Street critique could point toward limits on finance; neutral.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred from support for gun limits yet sources are silent on armed groups; neutral.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: The sources do not address soldiers refusing orders.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Sanders lists collective bargaining among New Deal gains, implying support.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Tax credits are not discussed; adherents prefer higher wages and direct programs but may accept them.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: International economic rules are not addressed in the sources.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Movement aims to win and use state power through elections.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Open experimentation with economic systems is not a theme of the trend, which has a specific policy agenda.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Inferred; the cohort and Sanders favor coalitions and no autarky is proposed.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Student debt relief is one of the few policy demands the Wikipedia article names for the trend.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Climate action is a named demand, but the sources do not say whether adherents want nature priced as capital; progressives are split between pricing and rights-based approaches.

sacred-nation.rationale: Inferred from the trend's secular, social-democratic and often internationalist outlook; the sources never treat the nation as sacred.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Inferred from concern with inequality; adherents focus on class more than on regional exploitation, and the sources do not address it.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Inferred from the framing of health care, education and a living wage as rights owed to everyone; the question of redesigning human nature is not addressed.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred from the trend's support for public provision and Nordic-style institutions; the sources do not name public broadcasting.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Secular generational politics with no religious doctrine; millennials are the least religiously affiliated cohort, so no lean is inferred.

farm-price-support.rationale: Inferred from the Sanders-wing preference for public protection of ordinary producers against finance; farm policy is not a named demand.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Inferred from the Sanders-wing criticism of military spending and war; arms control is not a defining issue.

workers-own-party.rationale: The movement works through elections inside the Democratic Party, as Sanders did, rather than a separate workers party.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred from the Sanders speech commitment to rights and equality for women; FGM is never addressed.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Equal rights for women are part of the egalitarian program in the Sanders speech; equal property rights are uncontroversial for this milieu.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Not an issue for this movement; no inferable lean.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: The movement wants strong government regulation and climate action, the opposite of leaving pollution to private lawsuits.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred from the movement commitment to elected, democratic government; chiefs are outside its US context.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Climate action is a named demand, but adherents stress civil liberties too; there is no stated trade-off rule.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Sanders criticises mass incarceration and the speech calls for criminal justice reform, which implies skepticism of fixed sentences.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Inferred from a pro-immigrant stance in the Sanders speech; a mandate is not a stated position.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Inferred from Sanders's pro-labour democratic socialism, which backs unions and workers' bargaining power; the speech does not address union dues directly.

voter-id.rationale: Inferred from Sanders's concern for expanding democratic participation and opposition to billionaire influence; ID rules are not discussed in the sources.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred from the trend's liberal and pluralist outlook; the sources do not discuss religion.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Sanders argues democracy needs economic as well as political rights and rejects oligarchic influence, so fair elections alone are not enough.

premarital-sex.rationale: Inferred from the socially liberal attitudes of millennials described in the polling sources; not stated directly.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from the trend's democratic and civil-liberties commitments; the sources do not address it.

negative-income-tax.rationale: The trend wants expanded programs such as Medicare for all and free college rather than folding welfare into one cash payment; inferred.

women-suffrage.rationale: Not discussed directly; inferred from the trend's democratic commitments and its Ocasio-Cortez and Sanders wing, which treat equal political rights as basic.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: The trend centres on economic policy and its sources say nothing on religion and women; adherents are likely split.

race-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from the socially liberal left of the trend and Sanders's speech on racial justice, which treats racial inequality as made by society.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred from the trend's progressive outlook and support for state action on equality; not stated in the sources.

missingStatements.text: Governments should cancel or relieve the student loan debts of graduates.
missingStatements.rationale: Student debt relief is one of the few policy demands the Wikipedia article names for the trend.

missingStatements.text: Large elections should be funded publicly rather than by private donors and corporations.
missingStatements.rationale: Sanders calls for public funding of elections and overturning Citizens United.

notes: Not a formal ideology: Ekins and others argue the cohort's support is for social democracy and a safety net, and many millennials favor free markets in the abstract. Most non-economic answers are inferences from the Democratic left and are low confidence.
